This page is retained for historical reference only. ## Current Vision (February 2026) ### One Sentence Build the quality reputation layer for the agent economy — starting with a capability marketplace that generates transaction data, evolving into the trust registry that every agent queries before transacting. ### The Thesis AI agents can now connect to any system via MCP, reason across multiple data sources, and take actions. Four open protocols are being built by trillion-dollar companies: MCP (agent-to-tool communication), A2A (agent-to-agent communication), Visa TAP (agent payment identity), and OpenID/IAM standards (agent access control). Together they solve communication, payment, and authorization. But they all explicitly leave one problem unsolved: **quality reputation and capability-based discovery.** The A2A spec literally punts this to implementers. Visa TAP verifies the agent *is who it claims to be*. IAM verifies the agent *is authorized to act*. But nobody verifies the agent *is actually good at what it claims*. That requires real transaction data from a marketplace. The giants can't build this because they don't run one. Strale is a capability marketplace that generates exactly this data. The endgame is the reputation layer every protocol participant queries before transacting. ### Strategic Principle: Don't Compete. Compose. Instead of building competing infrastructure, Strale becomes a **node in every network the giants are building**, then fills the gap they deliberately left open. - Visa/Mastercard are building *payment identity* for agents. We build *capability reputation* on top of their payment rails. - Ping Identity/WSO2/Okta are building *access control* for agents. We build *quality scoring* that their customers query after auth. - OpenID Foundation is defining *identity standards*. We implement those standards and add the reputation data layer they can't build. - MCP/A2A protocols handle *communication*. We handle *economic trust* — the layer that says "this agent is worth hiring." The giants build authentication (is it real?). We build reputation (is it good?). Authentication is table stakes. Reputation is the moat. --- ## Architecture: Three Composable Units Strale builds products as architecturally independent units that work together but could each stand alone. Each unit has its own API surface, data store, and standalone value proposition. This is not a plan to split the company — it's an architecture decision that preserves optionality. ### Unit 1 — Capability Marketplace (LIVE) **What it is:** SDK + API + wallet for developers to discover and call capabilities across 7 verticals. Already an MCP server with A2A Agent Cards. **Standalone value:** Developer tool. Like RapidAPI for the agent era. **Revenue:** Per-call pricing (€0.02–€1.00), prepaid wallet. **Data it generates:** Usage patterns, demand signals, capability reliability metrics, transaction quality data. ### Unit 2 — Agent Reputation Registry (BUILD NEXT) **What it is:** API that indexes A2A Agent Cards across the entire ecosystem and annotates them with quality scores from real transaction data. **Standalone value:** Any platform can query "how reliable is this agent?" before transacting. The Google of agent quality — A2A Agent Cards are web pages, Strale's registry is the search engine that ranks them. **Revenue:** API calls for reputation queries, premium analytics. **Depends on:** Unit 1 generating enough transaction volume to make scores meaningful. **Critical insight:** A2A explicitly delegates discovery/registry/reputation to implementers. [Solo.io](http://Solo.io) identified this gap publicly. First-mover window: \~6-9 months. ### Unit 3 — Commerce Protocol (EVALUATE LATER) **What it is:** The discover → negotiate → transact → verify → rate protocol for agent-to-agent commerce. **Standalone value:** The Visa network of agent commerce. **May not need to be built:** If A2A + Visa TAP + payment protocols mature, the commerce rails exist. Strale's endgame may be the reputation layer, not the commerce protocol. This is actually a stronger position — protocol-agnostic trust infrastructure. --- ## The Four Protocols Strale Integrates With **1. MCP (Anthropic → Linux Foundation) — Agent-to-tool communication** Strale is already an MCP server. Every MCP client (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, 300+ clients) can discover and call Strale capabilities as tools. 5,800+ MCP servers, ecosystem growing rapidly. **2. A2A (Google → Linux Foundation, v0.3, 150+ organizations) — Agent-to-agent communication** Agent Cards at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` for discovery. Google, Microsoft, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, Box, UiPath all building A2A support. Strale publishes Agent Cards for all capabilities. **3. Visa TAP (open on GitHub, RFC 9421) — Cryptographic agent payment identity** Agents sign HTTP requests with private keys. Partners include Stripe, Shopify, Adyen, Cloudflare, Akamai. Strale will accept TAP payments (build sequence step 16). **4. OpenID / IAM Standards — Agent identity and access management** Ping Identity, Auth0/Okta, WSO2 all shipping agent IAM. Standards still forming. Strale implements whatever wins, doesn't propose competing standards. ### What Nobody Is Building: The Quality Reputation Layer
Layer Problem Who's building it Strale's role
Communication How do agents talk? Google (A2A), Anthropic (MCP) Implement both
Payment identity Can this agent pay? Visa (TAP), Mastercard Accept their credentials
Access control Is this agent authorized? Ping Identity, WSO2, Okta Use their standards
Bot detection Agent or malicious bot? Vouched, Cloudflare, Akamai Not our problem
**Quality reputation** **Is this agent good?** **Nobody** **This is Unit 2**
--- ## Growth Model: Agent-Driven Purchasing Strale's primary growth mechanism is not human-to-human sales. It's agents choosing Strale at runtime without human decision. **How it works:** Agent has a task requiring external data → discovers tools via MCP/A2A → finds Strale capability → calls it → charges prepaid wallet → returns structured result. The developer sees the charge in their transaction log later. No sales cycle. **Exponential mechanic:** An agent framework's tool discovery mechanism lists Strale → every developer using that framework who builds anything touching European business data gets Strale capabilities suggested by their agent. The framework's adoption curve IS Strale's adoption curve. **Key workflows:** 1. Coding agents needing real-world data (live now — Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) 2. Research agents hitting anti-bot walls (step 9 of build sequence) 3. Multi-agent orchestrators procuring capabilities (6-12 months — CrewAI, AutoGen, ServiceNow) 4. Compliance-as-a-step in automated pipelines (August 2026 — EU AI Act enforcement) 5. CRM agents enriching leads (6-12 months — Salesforce Agentforce, HubSpot AI) --- ## Target Audience **Primary:** Developers and agent builders at any size company. Solo developer using Cursor, fintech engineer at Klarna, bank developer at SEB hackathon, consultant at PwC automating workflows. Company size is irrelevant — what matters is building with agents and needing capabilities. **Emerging buyer:** The agent itself, making autonomous discovery and purchase decisions via MCP/A2A. **Future (Phase 2+):** Business buyers — CTOs, engineering leads, procurement — who need to justify agent capability infrastructure to stakeholders. --- ## Competitive Positioning **We are NOT:** - A consulting firm (we don't do work manually) - An AI tool or copilot (we don't make humans faster) - An infrastructure provider (we don't host MCP servers) - A freelance marketplace (we don't connect humans to humans) - An agent authentication provider (Visa, Ping Identity, OpenID handle this) **We ARE:** - The **capability marketplace** where agents buy what they're missing at runtime (Unit 1) - The **reputation layer** that scores agent quality from real transaction data (Unit 2) - A **node in every network** the giants are building — growing with their adoption curves --- ## Not Doing - Not building agent authentication (Visa, Ping Identity, OpenID are handling this) - Not building agent access control (IAM vendors own this) - Not building bot detection (Vouched, Cloudflare own this) - Not proposing competing identity standards (adopt whatever wins) - Not racing to ship Unit 3 before the market is ready (2028-2030 at earliest) - Not selling to specific company sizes — the capability marketplace is size-agnostic --- ## Market Context - AI agents market: \$7-8B (2025) → \$50B+ (2030), \~45% CAGR - MCP ecosystem: \$1.2B → \$4.5B in 2025 alone - 5,800+ MCP servers, 300+ clients - A2A: 150+ organizations, Linux Foundation governance - Infrastructure funded: Smithery, Manufact (\$6.3M), Runlayer (\$11M), Alpic (€5.1M) - No quality reputation layer for agents exists yet — the gap Strale fills --- ## The Flywheel More capabilities → more agent discovery → more transactions → better reputation data → more trust → more transactions → attracts more capability providers → more capabilities. Once spinning, extremely difficult to compete with because reputation data compounds. --- ## Key Bets 1. **The reputation gap in A2A is structural.** The spec intentionally delegates discovery/reputation to implementers. This is an invitation, not an oversight. 2. **Composable architecture creates optionality.** Each unit can respond to market signals independently. 3. **Reputation requires transaction data.** The giants can't build credible agent reputation because they don't run a marketplace. Our marketplace is the unfair advantage. 4. **Ride, don't fight.** Every standard the giants ship makes our reputation layer more valuable. 5. **EU compliance is a structural weapon.** EU AI Act enforcement (August 2026) creates demand US competitors can't easily serve. 6. **Distribution via protocols \> marketing.** MCP + A2A + framework plugins create exponential growth tied to platform adoption curves. --- ## Change Log
Version Date What Changed Why
1.0 2026-02-24 Initial vision: three-phase delegation economy → reputation → commerce Project inception
2.0 2026-02-27 Composable architecture: three independent units. "Ride the giants" positioning. Market research showed giants building auth, nobody building reputation (requires transaction data).
2.1 2026-02-27 Protocol integration scaling (MCP + A2A + Visa TAP + OpenID). Unit 2 reframed as A2A Agent Card registry. Unit 3 may be unnecessary. A2A spec explicitly leaves discovery/reputation to implementers. Scaling shifts from marketing-driven to protocol-driven.
2.2 2026-02-27 Audience updated to size-agnostic. Removed 20-200 employee constraint. Agent as primary buyer. Pivot from delegation economy (SMB reports) to developer infrastructure (capability marketplace). Company size irrelevant.
